requests.question: May a setting switch off the check that stops a build when no lock is in force?
requests.answer: No. Garura's gate rules let a setting switch only a person's checkpoint; a check a play runs before it starts is one of the machine's walls and is never switched off. The way past the lock is a person's yes, not a setting.

trace.asked: what the gate switch may turn off
trace.found: only human checkpoints; pre-flight halts, sensitive-file blocks, stop-condition gates and eval failures are never gated

requests.question: Who may lock the design?
requests.answer: Only a person. Garura already leaves confirming a business intent and accepting a decision record to a person alone, as pinned steps; the lock is drafted the same way, with the product owner as the persona.

trace.asked: which steps only a person may take
trace.found: only a person confirms a business intent; only a person accepts a decision record

requests.play: reorganise business intents (#1021), BI-2 capability 6 draft

requests.question: May the lock stop a write to a position after the design is locked?
requests.answer: No. A rule stops work, never a write, so a position may change after the lock; the check finds the change by its fingerprint and builds keep starting from the locked version until a person locks the update.

trace.asked: what a rule of the product model may stop
trace.found: what a rule can stop is work, never a write

requests.question: How is an earlier lock kept when the design is locked again?
requests.answer: It is never edited; a new lock replaces it and the old one stays readable, marked replaced, as an accepted decision record is replaced by a new record and never edited.

trace.asked: how an accepted decision is changed
trace.found: accepted decisions are not edited; supersede or amend with a new record
